title: Where the Waters Divide
subtitle: Flat Clustering · k-means (assignment + choosing k)
story: They called themselves the Assay — an order of alchemists who held that all things could be sorted, grouped, categorized and clustered, so that the worthy could be kept and the rest poured away. To feed their great sorting engine, the Assay bled a whole valley of its water and tore from its people the Wellheart — an enchanted stone the valley-folk say will make any water clean, and which had kept their springs sweet for a thousand years. Their springs have run bitter ever since. The Assay are long gone now, and their engine — a waterworks at the bottom of a flooded shaft — is failing, its lower levels filling. You have come to take the Wellheart back and carry it home to the valley. But the engine mirrors its makers' conceit, and lets past only those who can work it as its makers did. Climb down its bridges and ladders, throw the diverters that turn the falling water aside, and reach the drowned floor before the water does. Take the Wellheart, and bring it back into the light.

done.title: The engine turns over
done.body: The last diverter grinds home under your hands, and deep below a sluice the Assay meant never to be reached gives way. The falling water finds new channels; the way down clears to the drowned floor. The engine is finishing the sort its makers died believing in — and the vault at the bottom, with the Wellheart sealed inside it, is finally within reach.

escapeDone.title: Out, and the Wellheart with you
escapeDone.body: You wade the rising floor one last time and understand the Assay's engine at last. The same two threads of water fell here every time you came down; only the gates above had changed, and with each setting they gathered into a different sort — split between two basins, split between another two, or run together into one. The water never decided how many kinds there were. The gates did. You set each setting against the sort it makes, the frame settles, and the vault yields. You lift the Wellheart from its cradle and climb the rising passage as the flood closes over the engine behind you — out under the stars, the Assay's cold conceit turned against them at last, and the vale's first clean water on its way home.

debrief.title: How this world worked
debrief.intro: The whole engine was one idea the Assay built into stone and water: flat clustering — sorting many things into a few true kinds by which they most belong together. Every font you answered was one move of it, every diverter an assignment, and the flooded floor was the result laid bare — the essences gathered into k groups, waiting only to be read. The Assay used the sort to decide what was worthy of keeping; you used the very same skill to walk out with everything they kept.

authoring.scenePrompt: This is a seamless 360-degree panorama from the middle of a narrow walkway of lashed planks slung across the open mouth of a tight stone well, with the night sky directly overhead. It is NOT a flat frontal elevation of one wall, there is no single-vanishing-point composition, and it is never a view of the room from outside it or from across it. Directly behind the viewer, split across the extreme left and extreme right edges, is the near rim wall, plain lichened stone, with the walkway's planks running unbroken across its foot into a notch cut in the rim: the far-left edge and the far-right edge are the two halves of this one surface and must match exactly in colour, texture, and lighting, joining into a single continuous, unbroken whole when the image wraps left to right. To the left, the nearer of the 2 streams: a heavy wooden flume runs in over the rim on timber trestles and ends in open air, and a broad glassy sheet of water pours off the END of that flume and falls away down the inside of the well wall, vanishing into the tangle a few yards below, flume and sheet one continuous run of water, a wide, smooth, unhurried sheet — heavy and glassy, no spray, no churn; just left of centre, the walkway itself, lashed planks on two heavy hawsers, running away ahead of the viewer to iron rings set in the opposite rim a few body-lengths off, where an iron brazier burns on its anchor post; behind the viewer its other end runs into a notch cut in the near rim and is lashed out of sight beneath the planks; creepers trail from its hawsers; just right of centre, a rope-and-timber ladder hanging from iron rings bolted into the walkway's own planks, dropping straight down into the tangle of ropes and flumes below; no falling water touches it: its rungs run clear and dry; to the right, the Assay's rim-station on the rim: a great iron RING-GAUGE standing upright like a ship's wheel, bolted to a stone post, a heavy coil of tarred rope on an iron cleat beside it, and a brass scale-pan hanging on a chain from the gauge's post, and beyond it, across the mouth, the second stream pouring from the end of its own trestle flume. entry.title: Deeper, a subtler test
entry.text: Lower, closer, the torches smoking under a heavy lip of rock. This font asks less kindly than the last: not how large a kind is, but how many true kinds there even are. The Assay set it to turn away anyone who could only count what they were handed.

authoring.scenePrompt: This is a seamless 360-degree panorama from the middle of a low landing tucked under a heavy overhang of rock in the wall of a tight, crowded stone well. This is an EQUIRECTANGULAR 360 panorama, not a flat photograph: the walls wrap continuously right around the viewer with strong barrel curvature, the ceiling and floor bow across the frame, and any surface toward the left or right of the frame is at the viewer's SIDE, seen at a glancing angle rather than face-on. It is NOT a flat frontal elevation of one wall, there is no single-vanishing-point composition, and it is never a view of the room from outside it or from across it. Directly behind the viewer, split across the extreme left and extreme right edges, is a plain stretch of wet rock under the overhang, crusted pale with lime, dark and even, with nothing fixed to it, the floor running unbroken across its foot: the far-left edge and the far-right edge are the two halves of this one surface and must match exactly in colour, texture, and lighting, joining into a single continuous, unbroken whole when the image wraps left to right. To the left, set round at the viewer's left side, with a broad stretch of plain wall between it and the wall directly behind the viewer: a rope-and-timber ladder made fast to iron rings in this landing, climbing the wall to the level above; no falling water touches it: its rungs run clear and dry; just left of centre, a gap cut through the landing's rim with a long ladder-and-plank descent hanging from it; a heavy column of water — one of the well's 2 streams — drops out of the tangle overhead and comes down THROUGH it, so its rungs and planks are plainly BEHIND the water and nothing could cross it, striking a jutting stone shelf a little below and bursting into a thick cloud of spray, a heavy unbroken column, striking hard and bursting into a fat cloud of spray; dead ahead in the centre, a low carved stone font glowing faint amber, and beside it this landing's signature: a row of stone SETTLING TROUGHS stepped one below the next, each spilling from its worn spout into the trough beneath, and a small wooden overshot water wheel turning under the lowest spout; just right of centre, a squat stone housing with a long iron lever, linked by an iron rod to a vane that stands IN an open copper chute running along the landing's rim; the chute empties straight into the mouth of a wooden flume just below the rim, so its water never falls free — lever, rod, vane and chute one connected machine; to the right, set round at the viewer's right side, with a broad stretch of plain wall between it and the wall directly behind the viewer: a short rope-and-plank bridge running level from two timber posts on this landing to the mouth of a cramped gallery in the wall close by, made fast at both ends; a curtain of water — one of the well's 2 streams — drops out of the tangle overhead and comes down THROUGH it, so its planks are plainly BEHIND the water and nothing could cross it, steady and unbroken. It is NIGHT, the same deep night everywhere in this world: no daylight, no dawn, no dusk. Smoky torches sputter in iron brackets along the underside of the overhang, their light hazed by spray, warm against the cold wet dark. The engine still RUNS by the Assay's own craft — its fires burn and its water moves — but no one has tended it in generations. The valley's living green is TAKING IT BACK: roots split the dressed stone, creepers hang in long swags off the gutters, ferns fill every joint, moss coats the wheels and rails, and patches of faintly glowing pale blue-green moss show in the damp. The menace is in the MACHINERY, never in the plants, which are lush and alive: iron grading sieves with toothed rims, brass scale-pans hanging on chains, hinged rejection chutes, iron sorting-baskets, calipers and clamps — cold, exact, built to measure and reject. Every surface is busy: wooden flumes on timber trestles and green-copper gutters carried along the walls on little stone arches like a miniature aqueduct run in every direction; here and there a great timber water wheel twice a man's height stands in the path of a flume, its buckets brimming; ropes are strung back and forth across from iron rings in one wall to iron rings in the opposite wall, hung with pulleys, chains, counterweights and baskets. ALL of the Assay's water is HELD — it runs inside flumes, gutters, pipes and wheel buckets, and passes from one channel to the next only as a short spill of less than a body's height, lip straight into mouth. The view is CLOSE and CLOSED: the low rock overhang hangs close over the whole landing, hung with roots and ropes, so nothing above can be seen; below, the drop is hidden by planks and the tangle of apparatus at the landing's edge. WHITE lime crust and flowstone hang frozen in pale stone draperies down the wall — hard white stone, not water. Palette: cold night blue-black stone, deep wet green, verdigris copper; firelight is the only warm, fully saturated colour, apart from the Assay's amber glow in its fonts and basins. Cinematic, dense and richly detailed, fine natural film grain. No people, no figures, no creatures, no lettering, no captions, no text, no numbers, no signage. The image is SHARP: no motion blur, no streaking, no smeared or doubled detail anywhere — everything in this picture is standing still, and any movement described is what the cinemagraph will add later, never something painted into the still. Fantastical and wondrous, NOT a horror scene: no skulls, no bones, no gore, no cobwebs, no bodies, nothing lurking. No daylight and no dusk light anywhere. EXACTLY 2 falls of water drop free through open air in this picture — the heavy column through the descent and the curtain across the bridge — and NO OTHERS. Every other drop of water runs inside a flume, gutter, pipe or wheel bucket, or passes as a short spill of less than a body's height from one channel's lip straight into the next channel's mouth. Each curtain of water falls squarely THROUGH the crossing it covers, never beside or behind it, and a crossing with no curtain has no water on it or directly above it. Every bridge and ladder is made fast at BOTH ends — nothing ends in mid-air. Each lever, its rod and its vane are one connected machine standing in its chute. Shot on a full-frame DSLR at 24mm, f/8, a long night exposure lit only by the fires and glows described, no daylight, high dynamic range, realistic depth of field, fine natural film grain, true-to-life colour. EDGE DISCIPLINE: the leftmost 6% and the rightmost 6% of the image must contain nothing but the plain continuous backdrop named above — no object, structure, post, path, fence, building corner, vehicle or figure may appear, begin or end inside those two margins, and no cast shadow may fall across them. Keep every object of interest well inboard. THE GROUND IS ONE SURFACE: the ground at the extreme left edge and the ground at the extreme right edge are the SAME patch of ground seen from the same standing point. Its paving, texture, colour, wetness and the base of anything resting on it must continue unbroken and perfectly aligned across that join, at the same height and the same scale on both sides. Again: the extreme left and right edges must align perfectly into a plain stretch of wet rock under the overhang, crusted pale with lime, dark and even, with nothing fixed to it, the floor running unbroken across its foot, with no visible seam, join, or repetition.

rooms.title: The drowned floor

entry.title: The drowned floor
entry.text: The long descent drops you into the risen flood on the cistern floor — knee-deep already and climbing — and there it is: the Assay's sorting engine laid bare, three great basins standing out of the water and the falling threads gathered into them. Across the flood the vault stands sealed, the Wellheart behind it. The gates you threw on the way down are still set. Learn what they decide before the water takes the floor.

rooms.technique: flat clustering — k-means (recognition: read the clusters)
rooms.debrief: The floor was the analysis made physical. The same two threads fell every time; the only thing you changed was how the gates above were set — and each setting sorted them differently: two basins one way, two other basins another, or both threads into one. So the number of groups was never a property of the water. It was a property of the settings, the question the machine was asking of it. That is k in k-means: not something the data hands you, but something you choose, and a different choice gives you a different, equally real grouping. Notice too that two of the settings made the SAME sort — once the second gate was thrown, the first stopped mattering at all.

authoring.scenePrompt: This is a seamless 360-degree panorama from the middle of the drowned floor at the foot of a tight stone well, standing knee-deep in still black water. This is an EQUIRECTANGULAR 360 panorama, not a flat photograph: the walls wrap continuously right around the viewer with strong barrel curvature, the ceiling and floor bow across the frame, and any surface toward the left or right of the frame is at the viewer's SIDE, seen at a glancing angle rather than face-on. It is NOT a flat frontal elevation of one wall, there is no single-vanishing-point composition, and it is never a view of the room from outside it or from across it. Directly behind the viewer, split across the extreme left and extreme right edges, is a plain stretch of black wet stone wall at the well's foot, dark and even, with nothing fixed to it, the flood running unbroken across its foot: the far-left edge and the far-right edge are the two halves of this one surface and must match exactly in colour, texture, and lighting, joining into a single continuous, unbroken whole when the image wraps left to right. To the left, set round at the viewer's left side, with a broad stretch of plain wall between it and the wall directly behind the viewer: a long ladder-and-plank descent hanging down the wall from the dark tangle above, its foot lashed to iron rings in a stone ledge a step clear of the flood; no falling water touches it: its rungs and planks run clear and dry; just left of centre, the knee-deep black flood running across the whole floor, mirroring the amber glow, lapping the outside of the basins' rims, a slow heavy heave, lapping and settling — a rising flood, not a current; dead ahead in the centre, THREE great round stone basins standing out of the flood in one line running left to right, each a broad drum of masonry with a thick rim at chest height, brimming with water lit deep amber from within — EXACTLY 3. Furthest LEFT and set plainly APART, with open flood between it and the next, the OUTER basin; then the MIDDLE basin; then, furthest right and nearest the vault pillar, the NEAR basin. EXACTLY 2 thin threads of water fall free out of the dark above — and in this view BOTH come down side by side into the NEAR basin, each entering inside its rim and striking its surface with its own rings; the outer and middle basins stand still and unfed, plainly holding water but with nothing falling into them; just right of centre, set into the face of the great pillar at chest height, an arm's length from the vault door's near jamb, a tall brass-and-stone reckoning frame — a plain grid of shallow square sockets, with plain carved lever-marks down its left edge and three small carved basin drums across its top; carvings only, no lettering, no numerals; to the right, set round at the viewer's right side, with a broad stretch of plain wall between it and the wall directly behind the viewer: in the face of that same pillar, a huge closed stone vault door, a single slab flush in its carved jambs, its foot drowned in the flood, shut fast. It is NIGHT, the same deep night everywhere in this world: no daylight, no dawn, no dusk. The three basins glow deep amber from within and that glow, doubled in the black water, is the main light; a few torches gutter on the great pillar by the vault. The engine still RUNS by the Assay's own craft — its fires burn and its water moves — but no one has tended it in generations. Overhead, the well closes into a dark, DRY tangle of old timber trestles, empty flumes and hanging ropes and roots, no water in any of it; the only water that moves in this chamber is the 2 threads and the flood. Moss and ferns grow thick on every ledge above the waterline, and patches of faintly glowing pale blue-green moss show on the wall. Pale SALT bloom creeps up every stone out of the water. Palette: cold night blue-black stone, deep wet green, verdigris copper; firelight is the only warm, fully saturated colour, apart from the Assay's amber glow in its fonts and basins. Cinematic, dense and richly detailed, fine natural film grain. No people, no figures, no creatures, no lettering, no captions, no text, no numbers, no signage. The image is SHARP: no motion blur, no streaking, no smeared or doubled detail anywhere — everything in this picture is standing still, and any movement described is what the cinemagraph will add later, never something painted into the still. Fantastical and wondrous, NOT a horror scene: no skulls, no bones, no gore, no cobwebs, no bodies, nothing lurking. No daylight and no dusk light anywhere. There are EXACTLY 3 stone basins and EXACTLY 2 threads of water falling free in this whole picture and NO OTHERS — no fourth basin, no extra pool, trough or tank, and no other falling or spilling water. The three basins stand in ONE line running LEFT TO RIGHT across the floor, the leftmost set plainly APART from the other two. Each thread falls wholly INTO a basin's rim: none lands on the flood, none between two basins, none shared. The flood laps the OUTSIDE of the basins' rims and does not spill in; it is ONE surface at ONE level. The vault door is SHUT. No lettering or numerals on the reckoning frame. The two threads stay crisp, separate and countable. Shot on a full-frame DSLR at 24mm, f/8, a long night exposure lit only by the glowing basins and the few torches described, no daylight, high dynamic range, realistic depth of field, fine natural film grain, true-to-life colour. EDGE DISCIPLINE: the leftmost 6% and the rightmost 6% of the image must contain nothing but the plain continuous backdrop named above — no object, structure, post, path, fence, building corner, vehicle or figure may appear, begin or end inside those two margins, and no cast shadow may fall across them. Keep every object of interest well inboard. THE GROUND IS ONE SURFACE: the ground at the extreme left edge and the ground at the extreme right edge are the SAME patch of ground seen from the same standing point. Its paving, texture, colour, wetness and the base of anything resting on it must continue unbroken and perfectly aligned across that join, at the same height and the same scale on both sides. Again: the extreme left and right edges must align perfectly into a plain stretch of black wet stone wall at the well's foot, dark and even, with nothing fixed to it, the flood running unbroken across its foot, with no visible seam, join, or repetition.

worldPlatePrompt: A single establishing world-bible frame of the Sorting Engine, built by the Assay, an order of alchemist-villains: one close, crowded view across a single level partway down a TIGHT stone well only a few body-lengths across, from one landing to the next. It is NIGHT, one deep night: no daylight, no dusk, no sky anywhere in the frame — overhead the underside of the level above is packed with flumes, ropes and hanging roots, and below the landings the drop is hidden by planks and apparatus. Everything is lit by fire: iron cressets in wall brackets, lanterns hung on chains, torches on every post, warm and close against cold blue-black stone. The engine still RUNS by the Assay's own craft — its fires burn and its water moves — but no one has tended it in generations, and the valley's green is taking it back: roots split the dressed stone, creepers hang in long swags off the gutters, ferns fill every joint, moss coats every wheel and rail, and patches of faintly glowing pale blue-green moss show in the damp. Wooden flumes on timber trestles and green-copper gutters carried on little stone arches like a miniature aqueduct run in every direction, every drop of water HELD in its channel; a great timber water wheel stands in the path of one flume; ropes run back and forth across the well from iron rings in one wall to iron rings in the other, hung with pulleys, chains, counterweights and iron sorting-baskets. The menace is in the MACHINERY — iron grading sieves with toothed rims, brass scale-pans hanging on chains over the drop, hinged rejection chutes that tip into the dark, calipers and clamps — cold, exact, built to measure and reject; the plants are lush and alive. Palette: cold night blue-black stone, deep wet green, verdigris copper, and warm firelight as the only warm, fully saturated colour apart from the Assay's amber glow in its fonts. Fantastical and wondrous, NOT a horror scene: no skulls, no bones, no gore, no cobwebs. Cinematic, dense and richly detailed, fine natural film grain. No people, no figures, no lettering, no captions, no text, no numbers.
